learning: Across eleven iterations, the robust gains were the forward row at y=0.08 m, a 0.012 m footprint, a wheel radius to track ratio near 0.4, and a shorter body. The slalom plateau at 0.16 to 0.20 did not respond to sensing, track, radius or mass, so it is probably a controller reaction-time limit, which this final design does not address.
notes: Consolidated final robot: the exact iteration 10 geometry and controller, which scored 450.6 with the strongest evidence (oval 20/20, s-bend progress 0.61). No untested change is made before the unseen-track race.
rationale: This is the final iteration, and the unseen-track race is scored on whatever design is delivered here. Iteration 10 (score 450.6) is the best-evidenced design: its oval finished 20 of 20 (mean 940, rms_error 0.0195), its s-bend finished 3 of 20 with progress 0.61, and its slalom progress was 0.20, the top of the 0.16 to 0.20 plateau. Every sensing, track, radius, mass and body change since then has either lowered the score or left the slalom flat. Iteration 8 (radius 0.040 m, track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.14 m) scored 417.9 with oval 19 of 20, and iteration 9 (mass 0.5 kg) scored 382.3, so those levers are not better. The body_length 0.10 m change in iteration 10 is the one that produced the best score. I therefore keep the iteration 10 geometry and controller exactly as tested. Untested controller changes such as kd 0.45 or a different line-loss mode carry risk on the unseen track with no race to check them. Expected result is about 450 on the development tracks, consistent with the iteration 10 evidence.
